newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium tumbles on LME pre-market, others drift.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium tumbles on LME pre-market, others drift.

text.p: Aluminium prices spiralled lower during early Tuesday LME trading as the market suffered a technical downturn after failing to extend Monday's advances, traders said.
"We are seeing some uneasiness in aluminium...People have been talking about $1,800 but we have to have a bit of a correction first," one said.
On the charts, the momentum indicators have strayed into overbought territory, with the RSI over 80 percent on Monday.
Early price levels around $1,744 were not sustained, with expected resistance around Monday's $1,747 22-month high not challenged.
Instead the market veered lower, with stocks falling a comparatively light 550 tonnes, triggering some expected profit-taking as well as investment bank sales.
Three months traded down to $1,715 before settling at $1,720, down $24 from Monday's kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation was around $6/9.
Elsewhere, other markets trended lower but activity was mundane and price movements were not particularly notable.
Copper eased from an early $2,287 to $2,280, down $2 from Monday, with stocks increasing by 2,925 tonnes. Inventory increases are expected to continue for the next few weeks at least, traders added.
Prices look vulnerable, meanwhile, and could test support at $2,250.
Zinc slipped back from an early high of $1,498 but remained comparatively stable despite another stock rise. Inventories were up by 1,900 tonnes on Tuesday.
However, the backwardation remains intense at $101/111 and prices will continue volatile through September. Three months was $1 higher at $1,495.
Nickel showed a steadier tone with the market keeping a cautious eye on the Falconbridge Sudbury strike, although this will have to continue for some time to have a market impact, analysts said.
Three months quoted at $7,240/60, against Monday's $7,215 close.

Lead was marked lower this morning and was some $8 easier at $627/30 a tonne. Tin was marginally softer at $5,570/85 a tonne while alloy was pulled down by primary. It was quoted at $1,515/25, down from a previous $1,534/44. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
